p17.label: Foggy prison cells of the Mirror of Soul Trapping

evidence.quote: DM: Okay. So we begin on Vindristjarna, some 70 miles off the coast of Chardon, drifting among a fog bank in the Gulf of Chardon, and as we begin we flash back to the people that you freed: Valius, Vargus, Vola, and Hektor, all recently released, or in some fashion or another, from the prison of the Mirror of Soul Trapping, or from the prison of the Crown of Purity, or both.

DM: We start with Valius, who, in that strange place where time seemed not to pass, was always vaguely aware that his brother was near him, even though his thoughts seemed as slow as molasses, and when he tried to speak, he wasn't sure if words came out due to the strange nature of time in that place. But he wasn't entirely insensate. He wasn't completely unaware. He did not miss the slow dawning awareness growing in his brother's eyes even in this weird cocoon world, where everything was dulled to near oblivion. This feeling of shock grew in his mind as he slowly realized his brother was free. How could this have happened, trapped in this place, he wondered? What could have broken those bonds of Fausto, the seemingly impossible to kill wizard, who had tied his mind in ribbons? Maybe just maybe, he wondered, those crazy bastards who had captured him did something to Fausto after all.

DM: Vargus, for his part, felt the transition as a fog lifting, not clarity exactly, for his thoughts still were slow and impossible to order, and he was barely conscious of his surroundings. But what replaced the fog was somehow impersonal, less obtrusive, not violating in the same way as that iron grip on his mind as had been— the 1st thing he was consciously aware of in this cocoon place was his brother Valius. Somehow, despite it all, Valius had stuck with him, had kept him from suffering this fate alone, had not hung him out to dry like their father had, leaving them twisting in the wind. His memories came back in pieces. 2 soldiers for hire, more interested in stories and ale than actually seeking employment, and Fausto and the Society of the Open Scroll and a blank— he couldn't remember. He had wanted to get out. Maybe Fausto was asking too much, but then something happened. He couldn't piece it together. Maybe it was this strange molasses in his brain impeding him from thinking. But he wasn't alone, so they'd figure it out somehow.

DM: Vola snapped to consciousness, angry. All she remembered was she had been betrayed. She could not clearly remember anything after telling Aegon of her concerns about Fausto, and then going with Aegon to speak to him and learn the truth. Strange figments of dreams haunted her, racing across the strange desert and assaulting a palace; toppling an iron crane in Chardon, spilling chalyte ore everywhere; a serene underground cavern filled with an otherworldly light. The thoughts felt slow in this strange, foggy place where she found herself. She wondered if this was some new terror devised by Fausto for her punishment. Had he killed everyone? Had he corrupted all of Chardon to his will? How had she ended up here? Doubts and confusion plagued her barely functioning brain. But that didn't matter now. She let her anger wash away the dreams. She knew she had been betrayed, and she would seek vengeance.

DM: Hektor drifted in a semi-conscious state. He had liked the new songs, the deep, humming songs that spoke of echoes underground, eternal stone, beauty and strength. They had washed away some of the older songs. He hadn't liked those older songs, the songs of subverdience, subservience, the thrumming melody that wouldn't let him think. He couldn't remember much before that 1st song. To be honest, it had broken his mind for so long singing of violence and control until he didn't move with conscious thought; he just obeyed the song. Not that he wanted to. He had no choice. But now he drifted in silence, each thought seeming to take an eternity to form. Maybe he was with the gods. But somehow he didn't think the gods would be this quiet.

DM: Sometimes, though, time sped up and he heard a voice. Was that a halfling sea shanty? It sounded so familiar. How did he know those words? Why did his hands twitch as if pulling on a phantom rope? When the voice went quiet, he tried to let his mind go blank in the silence, and just let memories slowly grow. The smell of salt spray, the feel of wind in his hair, the sway of a ship on a rolling ocean. He looked forward to that voice, for somehow he knew it brought the promise of his old self.

markers.reading: Retrospective vignettes follow the prisoners’ individual experiences in the mirror.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay. So we begin on Vindristjarna, some 70 miles off the coast of Chardon, drifting among a fog bank in the Gulf of Chardon, and as we begin we flash back to the people that you freed: Valius, Vargus, Vola, and Hektor, all recently released, or in some fashion or another, from the prison of the Mirror of Soul Trapping, or from the prison of the Crown of Purity, or both.

DM: We start with Valius, who, in that strange place where time seemed not to pass, was always vaguely aware that his brother was near him, even though his thoughts seemed as slow as molasses, and when he tried to speak, he wasn't sure if words came out due to the strange nature of time in that place. But he wasn't entirely insensate. He wasn't completely unaware. He did not miss the slow dawning awareness growing in his brother's eyes even in this weird cocoon world, where everything was dulled to near oblivion. This feeling of shock grew in his mind as he slowly realized his brother was free. How could this have happened, trapped in this place, he wondered? What could have broken those bonds of Fausto, the seemingly impossible to kill wizard, who had tied his mind in ribbons? Maybe just maybe, he wondered, those crazy bastards who had captured him did something to Fausto after all.

DM: Vargus, for his part, felt the transition as a fog lifting, not clarity exactly, for his thoughts still were slow and impossible to order, and he was barely conscious of his surroundings. But what replaced the fog was somehow impersonal, less obtrusive, not violating in the same way as that iron grip on his mind as had been— the 1st thing he was consciously aware of in this cocoon place was his brother Valius. Somehow, despite it all, Valius had stuck with him, had kept him from suffering this fate alone, had not hung him out to dry like their father had, leaving them twisting in the wind. His memories came back in pieces. 2 soldiers for hire, more interested in stories and ale than actually seeking employment, and Fausto and the Society of the Open Scroll and a blank— he couldn't remember. He had wanted to get out. Maybe Fausto was asking too much, but then something happened. He couldn't piece it together. Maybe it was this strange molasses in his brain impeding him from thinking. But he wasn't alone, so they'd figure it out somehow.

DM: Vola snapped to consciousness, angry. All she remembered was she had been betrayed. She could not clearly remember anything after telling Aegon of her concerns about Fausto, and then going with Aegon to speak to him and learn the truth. Strange figments of dreams haunted her, racing across the strange desert and assaulting a palace; toppling an iron crane in Chardon, spilling chalyte ore everywhere; a serene underground cavern filled with an otherworldly light. The thoughts felt slow in this strange, foggy place where she found herself. She wondered if this was some new terror devised by Fausto for her punishment. Had he killed everyone? Had he corrupted all of Chardon to his will? How had she ended up here? Doubts and confusion plagued her barely functioning brain. But that didn't matter now. She let her anger wash away the dreams. She knew she had been betrayed, and she would seek vengeance.

DM: Hektor drifted in a semi-conscious state. He had liked the new songs, the deep, humming songs that spoke of echoes underground, eternal stone, beauty and strength. They had washed away some of the older songs. He hadn't liked those older songs, the songs of subverdience, subservience, the thrumming melody that wouldn't let him think. He couldn't remember much before that 1st song. To be honest, it had broken his mind for so long singing of violence and control until he didn't move with conscious thought; he just obeyed the song. Not that he wanted to. He had no choice. But now he drifted in silence, each thought seeming to take an eternity to form. Maybe he was with the gods. But somehow he didn't think the gods would be this quiet.

DM: Sometimes, though, time sped up and he heard a voice. Was that a halfling sea shanty? It sounded so familiar. How did he know those words? Why did his hands twitch as if pulling on a phantom rope? When the voice went quiet, he tried to let his mind go blank in the silence, and just let memories slowly grow. The smell of salt spray, the feel of wind in his hair, the sway of a ship on a rolling ocean. He looked forward to that voice, for somehow he knew it brought the promise of his old self.
